newsitem.title: USA: Ariz. Palo Verde nuclear unit 1 seen on line Fri.
newsitem.headline: Ariz. Palo Verde nuclear unit 1 seen on line Fri.

text.p: The 1,221 megawatt (MW) Palo Verde 1 nuclear plant is expected to re-synchronize with the regional power grid Friday as it emerges from a refueling outage, an Arizona Public Service Co spokesman said Wednesday.
The unit will then gradually ramp-up to full power, probably reaching 100 percent capacity by early next week, he noted.
The Nuclear Regulatory Commission reported earlier Wednesday the restart process had begun and that the unit was testing at one percent of its rated capacity.
Unit 1 was shut for scheduled refueling September 21. Palo Verde's other two 1,221-MW units are operating at full output.
Arizona Power, a unit of Pinnacle West Capital Corp, is the plant's operator and holds a 29.1 percent stake in the Wintersburg, Ariz., facility.
Other owners include Edison International's Southern California Edison Co, El Paso Electric Co and Public Service Co of New Mexico.
